title: Krishna lifts the hill
hookLine: Indra sends a week of rain, and a boy lifts a hill over the village: why Hindus speak of taking refuge in God
carry: sharanagati: take refuge, and god holds the hill
tomorrow: why does Krishna vanish from the dance?

cards: The first rain on dry ground has a smell, and it often arrives to cheering. Somebody fries pakoras.

Charaka adds a gentle note: in the rains your inner fire burns low, so eat light, drink clean water, keep your feet dry and go easy. Now imagine rain that doesn't stop. Seven days of it, sent on purpose, by an angry god.
Today, the rains, and the hill that became an umbrella.

teach.b: The story is in the Bhagavata Purana. In the cowherd village of Vraja, everyone is preparing the yearly offering to Indra, king of the gods and lord of rain. The boy Krishna asks his father why.
Our living comes from this hill, he says, from the cows and the forest; let's honor Govardhan instead. They do, and Indra is furious.
He sends clouds that pour rain and hail on the village, with wind tearing at the cattle sheds. The people and the cows run to Krishna.
And Krishna, with one hand, lifts Govardhan Hill and holds it up like an umbrella.
Come under, he tells them, all of you, with your cows. For seven days, the text says, he holds it without moving, while the whole village shelters.
In the Bhagavata, Krishna gives his reason, paraphrased: these people have taken me as their refuge, and protecting them is my vow.
That's the teaching, plainly: sharanagati, taking refuge in God, a central idea in Hindu devotion. You don't earn shelter by being strong. You come under.
And notice what Krishna doesn't do. He doesn't stop the storm. The rain keeps falling for seven days; he holds a roof over everyone through it.
Many teachers read that as the shape of refuge: not a life with no storms, but someone holding the hill.
Hindus remember it every year at Govardhan Puja, the day after Diwali, often with a heaped mountain of food.
And in the rainy months, Chaturmas, many Hindus keep vows, and wandering monks stop traveling and stay in one place, the way the village stayed under the hill.

how: Hindus remember Krishna lifting Govardhan at Govardhan Puja, the day after Diwali, often with a mountain of food (Annakut); many Vaishnavas take refuge with the words Shri Krishna sharanam mama, and some keep vows through the rainy months of Chaturmas. People who follow Ayurveda eat light and keep dry in the rains.

games.q: the storm hits Vraja and the village runs to Krishna. what does he do?
o: lifts the hill and calls everyone, cows too, under it.
tells them to go and fight Indra themselves.
makes the clouds vanish in a second.
games.why: he holds Govardhan up for seven days while the rain keeps falling. that is refuge: not no storm, but shelter through it.

practice: Let sounds come and go like rain on a roof, and decide that for this sit you won't go anywhere, not even in your head to the next thing. Picture a roof over you that you didn't build.
If you pray, say Shri Krishna sharanam mama, Krishna is my refuge, as many Vaishnavas do, once, and rest under it. If you don't, simply let yourself be sheltered for a few breaths.

wordCard.voice: The seasons. In the rains, Charaka's low fire asks us to go easy, and the Bhagavata's seven-day storm shows Krishna holding the hill over everyone who came to him. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sharanagati, coming for refuge. In Hindu devotion, taking shelter in God.

carryVoice: Your line: sharanagati, take refuge, and God holds the hill. The rain may keep falling. I'll be here tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.24–25 (Krishna turns Vraja's offering from Indra to Govardhan; Indra's storm; Krishna lifts the hill and shelters the village for seven days; protecting those who take him as refuge is his vow, around 10.25.18)
Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 6 (varsha: the body weakened by summer, the fire further weakened by the rains; light food, boiled or rain water; keep dry; avoid exertion and day sleep)
Govardhan Puja and Annakut the day after Diwali; Chaturmas vows in the rainy months; the refuge mantra Shri Krishna sharanam mama (Pushti Marg)
